title: Dustdevils Rally From 19 Down to Beat Southwestern Adventist 76-74 for First Win
excerpt: Texas A&M International erased a 19-point halftime deficit to beat Southwestern Adventist 76-74 on Tuesday night at the TAMIU Convocation Center, earning the Dustdevils’ first win of the 2026-27 season.
content:
Texas A&M International erased a 19-point halftime deficit to beat Southwestern Adventist 76-74 on Tuesday night at the TAMIU Convocation Center, earning the Dustdevils’ first win of the 2026-27 season.

TAMIU trailed 46-27 at halftime, then outscored the Knights 49-28 in the second half to complete the comeback, according to the university’s athletics recap.

A late go-ahead three-pointer from Aaron Perez put the Dustdevils in front, and Southwestern Adventist cut the lead to one before Thomas Tangle’s free throw sealed the win.

Tangle finished with 16 points, seven steals, six assists and five rebounds, while Jalexs Ewing led TAMIU with 18 points. Rueben Doria scored a game-high 30 points for Southwestern Adventist.

TAMIU forced 20 turnovers and turned them into 24 points. The Dustdevils shot 33.3 percent and committed 12 turnovers before halftime, while the Knights shot 63 percent and made seven three-pointers in the opening half.

TAMIU is now 1-2 on the season. The game drew 90 fans at the Convocation Center, according to the official box score.

Sources: Texas A&M International University Athletics box score, Nov. 17, 2026; BVM Sports, Nov. 18, 2026.
